FACING THE FUTURE UNDAUNTED
Lady Eleanor Holles (LEH) is an independent girls’ day school in Hampton, south west London, for ages 7 to 18. A leading private school welcoming families from across Surrey, Berkshire and the surrounding area.
LEH is a place of curiosity and adventure, where enthusiastic and bright young minds are encouraged to be bold and undaunted in their thoughts, actions, and dreams for the future and to discover the scope of their brilliance.
Pupils are given the encouragement, inspiration, and opportunity to experience new things, to take risks, and to innovate as they grow and discover more about themselves. They do this in the warmth and safety of a caring school community with mutual respect and positive relationships at its heart. We are proud to be a values-driven school, where difference is celebrated, and everyone feels like they belong.
Visit us and discover LEH for yourself.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Strategy | Girls School Surrey | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
Facing the Future Undaunted
LEH’s Strategy to 2029
At LEH, we don’t just prepare our pupils for the future; we empower them to shape it.
Today’s world is fast-moving, complex, and full of both challenges and possibilities. Our role is to equip every pupil with the strength, skills and self-belief to thrive, and to lead in whatever path they choose. Character, confidence and capability are at the heart of how our students learn and grow, and the impact they go on to make.
Our new strategy, Facing the Future Undaunted, is the result of thoughtful collaboration across our school community. Pupils, parents, staff, alumnae and governors all played a part in shaping a vision that’s ambitious, inclusive, and distinctly LEH.
Together, we’ve identified four strategic objectives that will guide us in delivering an education that is exceptional, relevant and forward-looking.
Our girls are some of the most academically able in the UK. We will help them realise their potential in an environment that gives them the confidence to feel brave and undaunted about their future achievements and impact.
Our Strategic Objectives
1. A Bold Voice for Girls’ Education
We will lead the way in girls’ education, drawing on the latest research to shape best practice, push boundaries and influence the wider educational landscape.
2. Academic Excellence in Every Area
We will continue to deliver outstanding academic outcomes across the board, combining intellectual rigour with kindness, care and a culture of stretch and support.
3. A Culture of Success for All
We will foster an environment where every individual is empowered to succeed, where high standards, mutual respect and collective responsibility drive everyone to be their best.
4. A One-School Approach
We will harness the strength of being a connected community delivering a seamless educational journey from Junior School through to Sixth Form, with shared values and a united vision.
LEH School Values
We Choose to Succeed.
We Rise to Challenges.
We Lift Those Around Us.
We Encourage Personal Agency.
We Embrace Joy and Laughter.
This is more than a strategy, it’s a shared commitment to the future our pupils will inherit, and the role they will play in shaping it. With courage, curiosity and compassion, LEH girls face the future undaunted, and we stand beside them every step of the way.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Private School | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Lady Eleanor Holles (LEH) and thank you for taking the time to find out more about our remarkable school.
LEH is a place of curiosity and adventure, where enthusiastic and bright young minds are encouraged to be bold and undaunted in their thoughts, actions, and dreams for the future and to discover the scope of their brilliance. Pupils are given the encouragement, inspiration, and opportunity to experience new things, to take risks, and to innovate as they grow and discover more about themselves. They do this in the warmth and safety of a caring school community with mutual respect and positive relationships at its heart. We are proud to be a values-driven school, where difference is celebrated, and everyone feels like they belong.
Our curriculum is as broad as it is dynamic and is delivered alongside a varied programme of extra-curricular and enrichment activities. Our pupils have the chance to explore different interests and passions, to be courageous in their intellectual endeavours, and to bring their ideas to life while playing an active role in shaping their school. They go forward with the skills and confidence to enrich the world around them in the years that follow.
Our students achieve excellent results academically, but this is not what defines them or LEH. The best way to understand the culture and character of LEH is to see us in action. Come along to one of our open events, meet our wonderful pupils, teachers and staff and see, first hand, what makes LEH a special place to be. I’ve no doubt you’ll experience what I felt the first time I walked through our doors: that LEH is a happy, confident yet relaxed school, full of energy, determination, and hope for the future.
We look forward to meeting you soon.
About the Head
Rowena Cole joined LEH School as Head Mistress in September 2023. Growing up in Surrey, she was educated at a selective girls’ school before attending Exeter University where she read Biology. She was drawn to teaching due to the empowering impact of her own time at school and a deep-rooted love of her subject.
Mrs Cole has taught in both the state and private sectors: starting in the Biology departments at Howard of Effingham School and City of London Freemen’s School. This was followed by time as Head of the Biology department at Guildford High School from 2004 and then Deputy Head from 2008-2014, before taking the reins as Head at Dunottar School in Reigate in 2014. Mrs Cole also completed an MBA in Educational Leadership at the Institute of Education in 2014. After three years in post at Dunottar School, she was appointed Head at St John’s School in Leatherhead in 2017, where she led the school until August 2022.
Married with two teenagers and a menagerie of pets, she enjoys long walks with her two dogs and any opportunity to enjoy the sea be it swimming, paddle boarding, Scuba Diving or even learning, without much finesse, to surf.
I loved biology, and I always wanted to work with young people and to this day I feel grateful for the support and opportunities I had during my own education. I knew I’d thrive in a role where every day is different. Teaching combines all the things I love, and I’ve never looked back

pageCache.pageTitle: Wins, First Fixtures and Standout Performances - Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
A winning week on court, pitch and in the pool
It’s been another action-packed week of sport at LEH, with pupils representing the school across netball, football, lacrosse and swimming. From convincing victories and closely fought contests to first fixtures of the season and impressive performances in regional competition, there has been plenty to celebrate. Most importantly, our teams have shown tremendous determination, teamwork and sporting spirit throughout. Read on for all the latest results and highlights.
Netball
LEH v Surbiton High School
On Monday the U12 A,B and C team travelled the short distance to Surbiton to partake in their first after school fixture. The teams performed extremely well, especially considering this was the first time they had played together in these teams, and took convincing wins across all three games. Well done to the Players of the Match winners Ophelia, Martha and Aradhree.
LEH v St Paul’s Girls’ School
On Tuesday evening, our U15 A, B and C netball teams travelled to take on St Paul’s Girls’ School in a series of competitive fixtures. All three teams were involved in closely contested matches, showing excellent determination, teamwork and resilience throughout. Despite some fantastic passages of play and outstanding defensive performances, St Paul’s proved just too strong on the day, with all three teams losing their matches. Players of the Match congratulations to Maya, Anna, Bella, Chen and Izzy D. Well played, girls!
LEH v Godolphin and Latymer School
The U14 netball teams played Godolphin and Latymer School on Tuesday. The C and D teams displayed great determination and ability to stick to task to secure two strong wins. The A and Bs were challenged and continued to work on their connections at this early stage of the season. Well done to all the players who participated in the fixture but especially well done to the Players of the Match, Alice, Soraya, Ailsa, Grace and Lumia.
Sister’s n Sport Competition
Our U13A team had their next round of the Sister’s in Sport competition against Surbiton High School on Wednesday. They started strongly and played very well throughout the match to secure a good win 26-6. The team demonstrated good attacking and defensive skills, as well as fantastic teamwork throughout the whole match. Well done to all who played and to Emily who was awarded oppositions ‘player of the match’.
Surbiton High School also played our B and C teams in a friendly match. Our B team put in a determined performance against a strong Surbiton team, creating some excellent passages of play despite the loss. The C team played out an evenly contested match, coming away with a deserved draw. Congratulations to Arabella, Hannah, and Mary who were named Players of the Match.
Football
The U13 girls played their first league match of the season against Twickenham School. We made a positive start, taking an early lead and showing some excellent dribbling skills. Some fantastic saves from Raffey helped us stay ahead for much of the first half. Just before half-time, Twickenham finally broke through our defence, leaving the score level at 1-1. The second half saw some closely contested tackles, but Twickenham managed to break away on several occasions and take the lead. The match finished 5-2 to Twickenham.
Congratulations to Ottilie and Anya, who received the Players’ Player awards, and Vivian, who was named Coaches’ Player. A great effort from the whole team in their first league fixture. We look forward to our next match and the opportunity to build on this performance!
Lacrosse
LEH enjoyed a fantastic morning of lacrosse against Caterham, played in glorious weather and with a great spirit of competition throughout. Across all age groups, there were impressive victories, narrow defeats, and plenty of moments that demonstrated the strength and depth of the LEH programme.
Players demonstrated skill, creativity, and confidence across the pitch, producing crucial goals, defensive stops, and moments of brilliance that lifted their teams and showcased the talent within the squad. Quick ball movement, determined defending, and excellent communication helped produce some excellent passages of play and several hard-earned wins. Alongside the collective effort, there were several exceptional individual performances. Congratulations to all players involved on an enjoyable and successful afternoon of lacrosse against Caterham.
Swimming
A strong start to the year for our Junior, Intermediate and Senior swimming teams who competed in the London Regional ESSA relay heats in the hopes of qualifying for the National Finals in November. All three teams performed brilliantly with times exceeding our already high expectations. Well done to the team on some excellent races and we wait to find out on our results!

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama | Private School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
At LEH we’re serious about drama. Whether touring original productions to local primary schools, staging a West End musical with Hampton School, or running a show from behind the scenes, we offer every pupil the chance to perform, create and take part.
Recent productions have included an award-winning production of 42nd Street with Hampton School, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, as well as original plays developed through our Write the Girl initiative. This programme commissions professional playwrights to create new work for large female casts, giving our pupils the rare opportunity to collaborate with industry professionals from page to stage.
Enrichment extends beyond the stage. We host regular workshops with leading theatre companies such as Splendid and Paper Birds. Along with a lunchtime Drama club we run initiatives such as Monologue Mondays, a chance for budding actors to perform solo pieces, The Company, a joint Upper School Drama Society with Hampton School; a hotly-contested House Film Festival and our Our Theatre in Education tour which is designed to educate and inspire primary school audiences by using drama to explore key topics, as well as to bring stories from history and literature to life.
All of this takes place in and around our purpose-built 240-seat theatre, part of a vibrant Arts Centre that includes a rehearsal suite, 240-seat theatre, green room, seminar room, and the Music and Art departments – a true hub for creativity and performance.
Trinity Speech and Drama
Pupils can also develop their skills through our Speech and Drama programme, which offers one-to-one tuition in Acting, Prose, and Public Speaking. Many go on to earn top results in external exams – and valuable UCAS points – as they progress through LEH. Our Drama department has once again been awarded Trinity Champion Centre status, in recognition of our outstanding exam results, innovations in teaching and our excellent programme of performance events.
National School Theatre Awards Winner: Best Musical
Tes Awards Shortlisted for Best Creative Arts
240-seat theatre
80% Distinctions Trinity Speech and Drama Exams
Extra-curricular Drama
Drama plays a vital role in the life of the school, offering students opportunities to explore creativity, build confidence, and collaborate with others. Across all year groups, a rich programme of extra-curricular productions allows students to develop their performance skills both on and off the stage. From the imaginative energy of middle school productions to the more ambitious senior performances, each project fosters teamwork, discipline, and a love of storytelling. Highlights include the Middle School Musical, the student-led Write the Girl production, our Theatre in Education tour, and the senior school musical in collaboration with Hampton. Together, these experiences create a vibrant and inclusive drama community where every student can shine. During your time at LEH you could be involved in:
Drama is exciting and varied. Girls listed the seemingly endless productions and performances that they had enjoyed (as participants and spectators)...One pupil told us, ‘Taking part was the highlight of my school life.’
Pupils explore theatrical performance, write high-quality plays through the ‘write the girl’ initiative, create sophisticated artwork and develop their musical skills to a very high standard.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Private School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
LEH’s Music Department buzzes with energy, from our 21 orchestras, ensembles and jazz bands to our six choirs and rock groups and dazzling concerts. Musicians of all levels thrive here. We run a full programme of ABRSM preparation, and through our Friday Live! lunchtime events we give budding performers the opportunity to share their talents with the rest of the school.
Our state-of-the-art facilities include practice rooms, a Steinway Concert Grand piano, and a cutting-edge recording studio. From classical masterpieces to musical theatre hits, LEH’s music scene is vibrant and diverse.
Individual lessons cover a wide range of instruments – from flute to guitar, percussion to singing – inspiring every student to find their sound. We are also keen to explore any instrument that a pupil may wish to learn.
Senior School Curriculum
Music is a universal language that connects cultures and reflects the human experience, and its study nurtures creativity, emotional intelligence, and empathy. At LEH, all pupils study music in Years 7 and 8, with the option to continue in Year 9, GCSE, and A Level, where it remains a popular choice. Across all stages, our curriculum is built on the three pillars of performing, composing, and appraising/listening across a range of styles, allowing pupils to develop confidence, teamwork, and a critical engagement with music as both an academic and creative discipline.
Want to find out more?
MIDDLE SCHOOL CURRICULUM GUIDE
GCSE Music allows pupils to study a broad syllabus covering a wide range of different musical styles. The course develops your analytical, listening, and writing skills, deepens your theoretical and historical understanding, as well as enhancing your creativity and emotional intelligence.
Want to find out more?
Check out some clips from our bewitching Winter Concert
A school that lives and breathes music
Music at our School is vibrant, inclusive, and bursting with opportunity. With six choirs, a Symphony Orchestra, String Orchestras, Sinfonietta, Brass Group, Percussion Ensemble, Jazz Group, rock bands, and chamber ensembles, there’s a place for every kind of musician to shine.
Throughout the year, pupils perform in a wide variety of concerts — from polished formal recitals to relaxed informal showcases – all offering the chance to grow in confidence and share their talent. Parents are warmly invited to attend our popular Informal Performance Concerts, which give pupils invaluable solo and group performance experience in a supportive setting.
The Music Department also takes learning beyond the classroom, with regular trips to London concerts and musicals that bring the works studied in class vividly to life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Education Needs and Disability (SEND) | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
At LEH, we are committed to helping every pupil achieve her full potential. We work closely with families to identify and support any special educational needs as early as possible in a student’s journey with us.
Early Identification and Support
All new pupils take part in a screening programme to help us understand their individual learning profiles. Where needed, we offer follow-up assessments and tailored learning support through our experienced Learning Support Consultant Teachers and Assessor.
Most of the support we provide relates to mild dyslexia, ADHD and autism, but we take care to ensure that every pupil receives the guidance and resources she needs to thrive – both in and beyond the classroom.
English as an Additional Language (EAL)
We welcome students for whom English is not the first language. Where helpful, we offer support in school or may recommend external tuition to boost language confidence and fluency.
Working in Partnership
Parents are encouraged to contact the SEND Co-ordinator (Junior School) or Head of Learning Support (Senior School) with any concerns. We believe that open communication is key to ensuring each pupil is fully supported in all aspects of school life.
Inclusive Admissions
If a prospective pupil has a formal statement or EHCP, we will assess her needs carefully and positively. LEH is committed to making all reasonable adjustments to ensure a smooth and inclusive transition into school life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Art Textiles | Independent School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
See the world differently
Art at LEH provides girls with exciting new ways to engage with their world. Our lessons go far beyond technique. They spark creativity, critical thinking, emotional insight, cultural curiosity, and visual literacy – skills that transcend the studio and enrich every subject.
Art
Our curriculum is designed to help students make sense of what they see and hear, communicate what they think and feel, and bring to life what they imagine. We encourage awareness and empathy, helping pupils understand their own sense of identity, value and self-expression, as they develop personal responsibility within the school and the wider community.
Art at LEH is a shared journey of exploration. Together, students experiment boldly, take creative risks, reflect deeply, and refine their ideas. Through this process, they discover new ways to communicate and powerful new ways to connect.
Middle School Art
Middle School Art provides students with opportunities to explore, experiment, and develop their creative voices in a supportive and inspiring environment. Through a wide range of projects, materials, and artistic processes, students are encouraged to think imaginatively, solve problems creatively, and express their ideas with confidence.
Our curriculum celebrates individuality and curiosity, helping students to build technical skills while exploring personal interests, cultural perspectives, and contemporary issues. Students learn to observe, reflect, take creative risks, and embrace challenges, understanding that growth often comes through experimentation and perseverance.
In an increasingly digital world, creativity remains one of the most important skills young people can develop. Art encourages students to communicate visually, think critically, appreciate diverse viewpoints, and engage with the world around them in meaningful ways. The work produced throughout Middle School reflects not only artistic achievement but also the imagination, resilience, and unique perspectives of our students as they grow into confident and thoughtful creators.
Middle School Art & Textiles brochure
GCSE Art
GCSE Art provides an excellent opportunity for all pupils to develop their creative potential. The course is broad based and encourages the use of a wide range of technical processes and creative media. We foster critical and reflective thinkers who will develop a personal knowledge and understanding of historical and contemporary practice of Art, Craft and Design within the context of their own work. We nurture an environment of risk taking, resilience, commitment, imaginative and creative self-discovery.
You can view our wonderful GCSE pupil artwork below.
GCSE Art Booklet Online GCSE Art Gallery
Art Textiles
In Textiles, creativity meets craftsmanship. Pupils step into the world of the designer–maker, exploring how textiles shape everything from high fashion and interiors to cutting-edge materials and sustainable design. They research inspiring artists and designers, experiment with fabrics, fibres, and techniques, and develop their own original ideas into highly skilled final pieces. With a focus on innovation, upcycling, and sustainability, Textiles encourages pupils to think boldly, design responsibly, and bring their creative visions to life.

Learning that opens doors
At LEH, we believe that mastering languages is more than an academic achievement; it’s a gateway to the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: History | Independent School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
Foundation in Cripplegate
Lady Eleanor Holles was a 17th-century Englishwoman with a strong sense of philanthropy. When she died, her will stipulated that the ‘overplus’ of her estate, after specific bequests, be used for charitable purposes at the management of her cousin, Anne Watson. Anne chose to establish a charity school for girls, and ‘The Lady Holles’ Charity School’ was born. First housed in Cripplegate its purpose was to educate and clothe 50 girls aged 8–12, focusing on Christian teachings and domestic skills.
Growth and Expansion in the 19th Century
In 1832, the school moved to larger premises on Redcross Street, expanding to 100 girls and later adding an Infant and Industrial school. Following the Endowed Schools Act 1869, a middle-class girls’ school opened in Hackney in 1878, offering a broad curriculum and entrance exams. After a period of decline in the 1890s, the school rejuvenated, closing the elementary school in 1899 and improving facilities at Mare Street. By 1904, it became a public secondary school, extending education to age 17 and earning praise for its standards.
Relocation and Growth in the 20th Century
The school grew steadily, adding a sixth form by 1916 and expanding sports and science facilities. In 1936, the school relocated to Hampton, opening new buildings in 1937 with a fresh uniform and the motto of ‘Hope favours the bold’’.
War Years and Post-War Independence
During WWII, the school adapted to wartime challenges under Head Mistress Nora Nickalls, who led from 1915 to 1944. After the Butler Education Act 1944, the school chose independence over direct grant status, becoming fully independent in 1946.
Post-War Development and Modernisation
Ruth Garwood Scott (Head 1949–73) oversaw major expansions, raising academic standards and introducing a wider curricular and extracurricular activities, including athletics and music.
Margaret Smalley (1974–81) consolidated progress, and Liz Candy (1981–2004) modernised the school with new facilities, extended arts and sports programmes, with emphasis on confidence and community service alongside academic excellence. Gillian Low (2004–14) introduced Sixth Form enrichment and oversaw the award-winning Arts Centre. LEH celebrated its 300th anniversary in 2011. Under Heather Hanbury (2014–23), LEH enhanced resilience and wellbeing programmes, expanded bursaries, strengthened links with Hampton School, and opened our sister school LEH Foshan in China. Heather’s leadership earned national recognition before her retirement.
LEH today
In 2023, Rowena Cole became Head Mistress, supported by the senior team, leading LEH undaunted into the future. Under her headship LEH has unveiled its Facing the Future Undaunted with the vision of providing LEH girls with a distinctive education that prepares them to take their place at the table, in the room and in the world, in their chosen sphere within a culture that supports every pupil to achieve excellence and success, both shared and individual, to be fulfilled, and to have significant impact in every way she chooses.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers and Futures | Girls School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
Shaping bold futures
At LEH, we strive to build the best possible future for every student – empowering them with the courage to pursue their dreams. From the very start of Senior School, our girls are encouraged to think ambitiously about life beyond LEH. With expert guidance from our dedicated Futures & Careers Department and a dynamic calendar of events and initiatives, each pupil is supported to explore their passions, discover new possibilities, and take confident steps towards a future filled with opportunity.
Supporting every pupil’s career journey
Careers & Futures Evening
One of the highlights of the LEH calendar, our Careers Evening welcomes more than 60 delegates including LEH alumnae and current parents, who share invaluable insights and expertise from across a wide range of professions. Girls can engage with scientists, engineers, clinicians, architects, barristers, civil servants, and more. Global brands such as the NHS, Penguin Random House, Metropolitan Police, Apple, Reiss, the London Stock Exchange Group, PwC and Microsoft provide first-hand perspectives on their industries.
Higher Education Fair
Each year, the top 30 UK universities visit LEH to talk with students about higher education. From subject selection to crafting compelling university applications, students gain vital knowledge and inspiration as they consider the next stage of their academic journey.
Specialist Talks and Workshops
Our Careers & Futures Department hosts a wide range of talks throughout the year, covering topics from Women in Engineering and Applying to Medical School, to Sponsored Degree Programmes and an Introduction to Investment Banking. These sessions, often led by industry professionals, give students a realistic and inspiring picture of potential career paths.
Applying to American Universities
We offer tailored support for students interested in studying in the US, including advice on the application process, financial aid, and sports or academic scholarships. We regularly invite LEH alumnae who have studied in America to share their experiences, and we partner with Hampton School to offer preparation courses for the ACT admissions test.
Sixth Form
Our tailored Sixth Form Futures Programme equips students with the skills, knowledge and confidence to navigate university applications and beyond. From personal statement support and interview preparation to networking opportunities with professionals, LEH students are well prepared for life after school. Parents and alumnae continue to play an important role by sharing their career insights at talks and events throughout the year.
Future Destinations
LEH students go on to study at some of the most prestigious universities in the UK and around the world. The range of universities and course choices is a testament to the ambition and success of our students.
Business links and work experience
Our extensive network of industry experts and alumnae gives LEH students an unrivalled head start. Whether it’s through inspiring talks, one-to-one mentoring, or immersive career events, our pupils benefit from real-world insights, insider knowledge, and connections that open doors from day one. From Year 11 (Upper Fifth), all pupils are encouraged to take part in work experience and professional placements. Our LEH Work Experience Coordinator supports with finding the perfect match.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport | Private School Hampton | Lady Eleanor Holles
pageCache.text:
Undaunted.
If sport is your thing, LEH offers an exceptional breadth of opportunities to get involved, stay active, and push your potential. Our outstanding facilities – including a state-of-the-art sports centre, floodlit pitches, boat house, and 25-metre indoor pool – are set within 24 acres of beautiful grounds, providing the perfect environment for training, competition, and enjoyment at every level.
Whether you’re playing socially or pursuing sport at the highest level, there’s something for everyone. Students can choose from a wide variety of activities, from rowing, lacrosse, and netball to fencing, gymnastics, and strength and conditioning. Our core sports – netball, lacrosse, and rowing – are supported by expert coaching and a full calendar of fixtures, tournaments, and training camps.
We’re incredibly proud of our student athletes, who regularly represent England and Great Britain in sports such as gymnastics, swimming, lacrosse, and rowing – a testament to LEH’s commitment to sporting excellence. But just as importantly, we believe in the lifelong benefits of sport for wellbeing, confidence, and teamwork.
Whether you’re aiming high or playing for fun, LEH supports your passion every step of the way.
Sixth Form Prospectus
A level Physical Education
A Level Physical Education is an exciting and varied course that combines science, psychology, performance and the social impact of sport. It is ideal for students who enjoy sport and want to understand what influences athletic performance both physically and mentally.
Students will explore how the body responds to exercise, how skills are learned and developed, how psychological factors affect performance, and the role sport plays in modern society. The course offers a balance of academic study and practical application, making it an engaging option for students who enjoy both theory and sport. Physical Education develops valuable analytical, communication and evaluation skills that are highly regarded by universities and employers.
Find out more
A level Course Guide
TALENTED & ASPIRING ATHLETE PROGRAMME (TAP)
LEH’s Talented & Aspiring Athlete Programme (TAP) is a unique initiative designed to support and nurture the dreams of our student-athletes. Whether your child is a sailor, gymnast, rower, netball player, or participates in another sport, TAP aims to provide a top-tier, development-focused environment that helps athletes take their performance to the next level.
LEH Rowing
Rowing at LEH is far more than just a sport – it’s a vibrant, supportive community built on trust, commitment, and true teamwork. With exceptional facilities and expert coaching, our athletes grow in confidence, resilience, and ambition from Year 8 (Lower 4) all the way through to Sixth Form. Along the way, they’ll forge strong friendships, develop a competitive mindset, and experience what it means to be part of a crew where every girl is invested in one another’s success.
Becoming part of the Sixth Form rowing club means joining a community where accountability, encouragement, and camaraderie extend well beyond the water. Our dedicated coaches support each rower’s progress, turning every session into an opportunity to strengthen skills and self-belief in a friendly, motivating setting.

pageCache.text:
The Futures Advisory Group
Bold Futures Start Here.
The Futures Advisory Group is comprised of parents and alumnae who have volunteered to share their skills to advise and mentor our students. We are extremely grateful for their generosity in giving time and expertise. The group meets once a term.
If you would like to join the Group, or for more information on what group membership involves, please contact Rachel Hart, Head of Futures.
For more information on the events and opportunities offered to students, please visit the careers page.
Email the Futures & Careers Department
Mentoring students and alumnae
If you are able to provide careers advice or assistance to current Upper Sixth students and our alumnae, please join our alumnae network, Holles Connect, and register yourself as a mentor. Depending on your availability and interest, this could be anything from providing an internship opportunity or holding a talk in school, to a quick message of support or checking a CV. On joining Holles Connect, you will be prompted to answer questions on your career field, experience and the areas in which you would be willing to help.
All support is greatly appreciated and of high value to both past and present students.
